# package jsonmsg

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/jsonmsg"
```

Package jsonmsg implements the JSON message mapping of OPC UA PubSub (Part 14 §7.2.5): NetworkMessages and DataSetMessages ("ua-data"), DataSetMetaData messages ("ua-metadata"), status messages ("ua-status") and the messages of PubSub Actions ("ua-action-request", "ua-action-response", "ua-action-metadata", "ua-action-responder").

#### Wire shapes {#hdr-Wire_shapes}

A NetworkMessage with the NetworkMessageHeader bit of its [ua.JSONNetworkMessageContentMask](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#JSONNetworkMessageContentMask) is an object

	{"MessageId":"..","MessageType":"ua-data","PublisherId":"..",
	 "WriterGroupName":"..","DataSetClassId":"..","Messages":[..]}

whose Messages member is an array of DataSetMessages, or a single DataSetMessage object with the SingleDataSetMessage bit. Without the NetworkMessageHeader bit the message is just the content of Messages. A DataSetMessage with the DataSetMessageHeader bit is an object

	{"DataSetWriterId":1,"DataSetWriterName":"..","PublisherId":"..",
	 "WriterGroupName":"..","SequenceNumber":1,"MetaDataVersion":{..},
	 "MinorVersion":1,"Timestamp":"..","Status":{..},
	 "MessageType":"ua-keyframe","Payload":{"Field":..}}

with the members its [ua.JSONDataSetMessageContentMask](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#JSONDataSetMessageContentMask) selects; without the bit it is the Payload object alone.

The fields of the Payload are written as the [ua.DataSetFieldContentMask](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#DataSetFieldContentMask) of the DataSetMessage asks: as a Variant ({"UaType":7,"Value":27}) when no bit is set, as a DataValue ({"UaType":7,"Value":27,"Status":.., "SourceTimestamp":..}) when one of the StatusCode, timestamp or picoseconds bits is set, and as the bare value (27) with the RawData bit. The values use the Compact JSON encoding of OPC UA 1.05.04 (see [ua.EncodeJSON](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#EncodeJSON)), or the Verbose encoding when the FieldEncoding2 bit of the DataSetMessage content mask is set.

#### Actions {#hdr-Actions}

A NetworkMessage with [message.NetworkMessage.Action](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/message#NetworkMessage.Action) set is a message of PubSub Actions (Part 14 §7.2.5.6 in 1.05), always an object with header,

	{"MessageId":"..","MessageType":"ua-action-request","PublisherId":"..",
	 "Timestamp":"..","ResponseAddress":"..","CorrelationData":"..",
	 "RequestorId":"..","TimeoutHint":1500,"Messages":[..]}

whose PublisherId is the one of the Responder, and whose Messages are ActionRequest or ActionResponse DataSetMessages with header,

	{"DataSetWriterId":1,"ActionTargetId":2,"DataSetWriterName":"..",
	 "WriterGroupName":"..","MetaDataVersion":{..},"Timestamp":"..",
	 "Status":{..},"MessageType":"ua-action-response","RequestId":7,
	 "ActionState":2,"Payload":{"Out":..}}

DataSetWriterId, ActionTargetId, RequestId, ActionState and Payload are always written, Status in responses; the other DataSetMessage members follow the JSONMask of the DataSetMessage. The fields of the Payload are Variants, or bare values with the RawData bit of the FieldContentMask (DataValue fields are not allowed, §7.2.5.6.2). The ActionState is the number of the Compact encoding; Decode also accepts the Verbose form ("Executing\_1") and the bare name.

#### PublisherId {#hdr-PublisherId}

Part 14 (1.05) encodes the PublisherId as a JSON string whatever its type, and so does open62541. Encode writes numeric PublisherIds as strings ("65535") unless [EncodeOptions.NumericPublisherID](#func-encodeoptions-numericpublisherid) is set. Decode accepts a string or a number; a string of decimal digits is decoded as a UInt64 PublisherId (as open62541 does), any other string as a String PublisherId. Compare decoded PublisherIds with the configured one by their String form.

#### Interoperability with open62541 1.5 {#hdr-Interoperability_with_open62541_1_5}

open62541 always writes the network message header with MessageId (null when it has none), MessageType and PublisherId (as a string), always writes Messages as an array and always writes DataSetWriterId and MessageType "ua-keyframe" in its DataSetMessages, whatever the content masks say. It reads only key frames, and it rejects a SequenceNumber or a Status above 65535 because it keeps both in 16 bits. Decode accepts everything it writes (including the null MessageId and Status as a bare number).

## Functions

### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte, opts *DecodeOptions) (*message.NetworkMessage, error)
```

Decode decodes a "ua-data" JSON NetworkMessage, or the content of its Messages member when the publisher omitted the network message header: an array of DataSetMessages, a single DataSetMessage, or a bare Payload object.

The masks of the result report what was found: nm.JSONMask has the NetworkMessageHeader bit if the header was present, the DataSetMessageHeader bit if the DataSetMessages had a header, the SingleDataSetMessage bit if Messages was an object; each DataSetMessage's JSONMask has the bits of its header members and FieldContentMask the encoding of its fields (no bit for Variant fields, the DataValue bits found, RawData for bare values).

With opts.MetaData the fields of a DataSetMessage are matched to the DataSetMetaData of its writer by name: Field.Index is the position in the metadata, the fields are sorted by it, RawData fields get the type of the metadata, and a field the metadata does not know is an error. Without metadata Field.Index is the position in the Payload and RawData fields are typed after their JSON form (Boolean, Int64, Double, String or arrays of these; other values are kept as their JSON text in a String).

A well-formed message of another type returns an [\*UnsupportedMessageTypeError](#type-unsupportedmessagetypeerror); malformed input returns an error wrapping ErrDecode. Decode never panics.

### func DecodeAny

```go
func DecodeAny(b []byte, opts *DecodeOptions) (interface{}, error)
```

DecodeAny decodes a JSON PubSub message of any supported type: it returns a \*message.NetworkMessage for "ua-data" (and messages without network message header), "ua-action-request" and "ua-action-response", a \*MetaDataMessage for "ua-metadata", a \*StatusMessage for "ua-status", an \*ActionMetaDataMessage for "ua-action-metadata" and an \*ActionResponderMessage for "ua-action-responder". Other types return an [\*UnsupportedMessageTypeError](#type-unsupportedmessagetypeerror).

### func Encode

```go
func Encode(nm *message.NetworkMessage, opts *EncodeOptions) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode encodes a NetworkMessage of type NetworkMessageDataSet as a "ua-data" JSON message, following nm.JSONMask and the JSONMask and FieldContentMask of each DataSetMessage, or, with nm.Action set, as a "ua-action-request" or "ua-action-response" message (see Actions in the package documentation).

With the NetworkMessageHeader bit a missing MessageID is generated (it is mandatory). Without the NetworkMessageHeader bit the result is the array of DataSetMessages, or the single DataSetMessage with the SingleDataSetMessage bit. The SingleDataSetMessage bit requires exactly one DataSetMessage.

### func EncodeActionMetaData

```go
func EncodeActionMetaData(m *ActionMetaDataMessage, opts *EncodeOptions) ([]byte, error)
```

EncodeActionMetaData encodes a "ua-action-metadata" message:

	{"MessageId":"..","MessageType":"ua-action-metadata","PublisherId":"..",
	 "DataSetWriterId":100,"DataSetWriterName":"..","Timestamp":"..",
	 "ActionTargets":[..],"Request":{..},"Response":{..},"ActionMethods":[..]}

DataSetWriterName and ActionMethods are omitted when empty, a zero Timestamp is the current time; the structures use the Compact encoding.

### func EncodeActionResponder

```go
func EncodeActionResponder(m *ActionResponderMessage, opts *EncodeOptions) ([]byte, error)
```

EncodeActionResponder encodes a "ua-action-responder" message:

	{"MessageId":"..","MessageType":"ua-action-responder","PublisherId":"..",
	 "Timestamp":"..","Connection":{..}}

A zero Timestamp is the current time; Connection uses the Compact encoding.

### func EncodeMetaData

```go
func EncodeMetaData(m *MetaDataMessage, opts *EncodeOptions) ([]byte, error)
```

EncodeMetaData encodes a "ua-metadata" message:

	{"MessageId":"..","MessageType":"ua-metadata","PublisherId":"..",
	 "DataSetWriterId":1,"WriterGroupName":"..","DataSetWriterName":"..",
	 "Timestamp":"..","MetaData":{..}}

The names and the Timestamp are omitted when empty; MetaData is encoded with the Compact encoding.

### func EncodeStatus

```go
func EncodeStatus(m *StatusMessage, opts *EncodeOptions) ([]byte, error)
```

EncodeStatus encodes a "ua-status" message:

	{"MessageId":"..","MessageType":"ua-status","PublisherId":"..",
	 "Timestamp":"..","IsCyclic":true,"Status":2,"NextReportTime":".."}

The timestamps are omitted when zero.

### func MessageType

```go
func MessageType(b []byte) (string, error)
```

MessageType returns the MessageType of a JSON message: "ua-data", "ua-metadata", ..., or for a message without network message header the DataSetMessage type ("ua-keyframe", ...) or "" if it has none.

### type DecodeOptions

```go
type DecodeOptions struct {
	// MetaData supplies the DataSetMetaData of a writer, needed to order
	// fields and to type RawData fields.
	MetaData       message.MetaDataLookup
	NamespaceArray []string

	// DataSetWriterID is used for DataSetMessages that carry no
	// DataSetWriterId (the subscriber knows the writer from the topic).
	DataSetWriterID uint16
	// PublisherID is used for messages that carry no PublisherId.
	PublisherID *message.PublisherID

	// Limits; zero selects the defaults.
	MaxMessageSize     int
	MaxDataSetMessages int
	// MaxFields is capped at DefaultMaxFields (65535), the most a UInt16
	// field index can number.
	MaxFields int
}
```

DecodeOptions control the decoders.

### type EncodeOptions

```go
type EncodeOptions struct {
	// NamespaceArray, if set, makes NodeIds in values use namespace URIs.
	NamespaceArray []string
	// MetaData, if set, supplies the field names of fields whose Name is
	// empty (by their Index).
	MetaData message.MetaDataLookup
	// NumericPublisherID writes numeric PublisherIds as JSON numbers, as
	// some 1.04 implementations expect, instead of the strings of Part 14
	// 1.05 that open62541 writes and expects.
	NumericPublisherID bool
}
```

EncodeOptions control the encoders.

### type UnsupportedMessageTypeError

```go
type UnsupportedMessageTypeError struct {
	MessageType string
}
```

UnsupportedMessageTypeError is returned for a well-formed message of a type this package does not decode (ua-application, ua-endpoints, ua-connection, ...), or of a type the called function does not handle (a "ua-metadata" message passed to Decode).
